short_answer: King Creole is a real, long running handicapper with a named person behind it. Victor King's bio appears on Pregame and on Marc Lawrence's Playbook site, and Playbook's own 2025 preseason paper calls him a sports data and research analyst for all Playbook publications. He sells football picks on Pregame.com and writes the Playbook NFL Totals Tipsheet, a weekly newsletter on NFL over/unders.

His record is unusually easy to look up, because The Sports Monitor of Oklahoma, an outside tracking service, lists his season results. That record is up and down. In 2026 so far it shows 18-15 in the NFL and 23-8 in college football, almost all overs. But the NFL seasons of 2022, 2024 and 2025 were losing ones (38-53, 31-43-1 and 33-44-1), and adding NFL and college football from 2022 to now gives 259-273-4 by our sum, under 50%.

So this is a legitimate seller with a public paper trail, not a proven long run winner. If you buy, the cheaper Tipsheet lets you see his work for $11 an issue, and the Monitor lets you check results yourself.

guarantee: We found no money back promise or win guarantee on any King Creole offer we read, on Pregame or on Playbook.

Pregame's terms of service say "THE SERVICE, CONTENT, AND SITE ARE PROVIDED ON AN "AS IS" BASIS. USE OF THE SERVICE IS AT YOUR OWN RISK." Pregame's FAQ mentions one program of its own, an "opposite side insurance" for buyers who bought two handicappers on opposite sides of the same game, and tells buyers to contact support@pregame.com about it.
We found no refund terms on the Playbook pages we read. Treat every purchase as final unless the seller tells you otherwise in writing.

claims_note: The Pregame page picks which slices of the record to show: all time NFL sides, this season's college totals, units this season. The Sports Monitor, by contrast, shows every season and both wins and losses, and some of those seasons were bad.

The Pregame list and the Monitor log did not match on 15 Nov 2026: the Monitor graded one more play, a loss. We could not tell whether that play was sold on Pregame, so before you buy, ask which plays count toward the advertised record.
record: What an outside tracker shows: The Sports Monitor of Oklahoma lists King Creole picks with date, line, odds, star rating and result. Regular season results we pulled on 19 Nov 2026: NFL 2022 38-53, 2023 39-28-1, 2024 31-43-1, 2025 33-44-1, 2026 so far 18-15. College football 2022 18-16, 2023 14-23, 2024 31-23, 2025 14-20-1, 2026 so far 23-8. Added up, that is 259-273-4, about 48.7% winners. The Monitor's own profit column, which sizes each play by its rating, sums to about minus $23,587 over the same seasons, with 2023 NFL, 2022 and 2024 college and both 2026 sports in profit.

The 2026 run is real on that log and it is mostly overs. Of the 64 graded football plays this season, 49 were overs. At one unit to win per play and the odds shown, we count +1.4 units in the NFL (18-15) and +14.0 units in college football (23-8).

What the seller shows: Pregame listed the last ten plays (6 to 15 Nov 2026), which we count as 7-3, and a last 30 days table of 6-2 in college football and 4-2 in the NFL for rated picks. Pregame is both the store and the scorekeeper for those numbers.

The newsletter is tracked separately by a TheRX forum member at the lines printed in each issue. That tally had the 2025 Tipsheet at 45-45-1 across its 3 star, 2 star, 1 star and team total plays, and the 2026 Tipsheet at 16-24 by 10 Nov 2026, with 2 star Team Totals of the Week at 2-12. We did not check these numbers against the issues.

our_data.text: In this edition no King Creole pick is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how King Creole performs beyond the outside records quoted above.

customers_intro: We found little buyer talk about King Creole. What exists is on TheRX, where bettors share and track football newsletters, from 2017 to 2026. We found no Reddit thread (the archive's search timed out), no review site sample we could open and no complaint record.

customers.text: About half a dozen relevant TheRX posts from 2017, 2023 and 2026, plus a member's season tallies. The pattern: readers treat the Totals Tipsheet as a serious, data heavy source and some bet its top plays, while others see a break even record. In 2017 one bettor said their only bet of the week was a big one on the Tipsheet's top rated under, and a member who looked up the Pregame records called them break even with no value. A member's tally at printed lines had the 2025 Tipsheet at 45-45-1 and the 2026 issues at 16-24 by 10 Nov 2026. His premium picks also get copied into free forum threads. We found no refund complaints, chargebacks or regulator actions.

On TheRX a bettor wrote that their one bet that week was a big bet on a Giants and 49ers under, the top rated pick in Victor King's Totals Tipsheet. They quoted a member's tracking of the Tipsheet at 6-3 on 3 star plays and 8-9-1 on 2 star plays that season.

In the same thread another member looked up King Creole's Pregame records for that season, about 12-12 in college football and 25-23 in the NFL, and called it "Breakeven no value". They also doubted any site whose picks cannot be seen until after the game starts.
A long time member replied to that criticism dismissively, without giving any numbers of their own.

In a TheRX newsletter thread a member reposted a paid King Creole 4 star Over of the Week (Falcons and Lions over 46), taken from the forum's service plays section. It shows that at least some paid King Creole plays end up shared free on forums.

A TheRX member who grades newsletter plays at the printed line posted final 2025 numbers through the Super Bowl: Tipsheet 3 star 9-11, 2 star 17-17, Team Total of the Week 2 star 17-14-1 and 1 star 2-3. That is 45-45-1 overall, below the 52.4% needed at -110. We did not verify the tally.

The same member's 2026 tally had the Tipsheet at 5-4 on 3 star plays, 7-8 on 2 star plays and 2-0 on 1 star Team Totals, with 2 star Team Totals of the Week at 2-12, and listed that 2-12 among the season's worst records. We did not verify the tally.

We found no Better Business Bureau profile, no app store listing, no court or regulator record and no Covers or Sportsbook Review thread about King Creole. Our Reddit search through the Arctic Shift archive timed out on the large betting forums and returned nothing on the smaller ones, so it is incomplete.

conflicts: Pregame sells King Creole picks, grades them and shows the record tables in the ads. The store and the scorekeeper are the same company.
Victor King works for Marc Lawrence's Playbook as a data and research analyst, and Playbook sells his Tipsheet. Playbook's newsletter promoting the Tipsheet is not an independent review of it.
The Sports Monitor of Oklahoma is a separate tracking service, which is why we lean on it here. We could not check whether every Pregame pick appears in its log.
strengths: A named person with a long, consistent bio across Pregame, Playbook and Playbook's printed newsletter.
An outside tracker, The Sports Monitor of Oklahoma, lists his plays with line, odds, rating and result for many seasons, including the losing ones.
A strong 2026 so far on that tracker: 23-8 in college football and 18-15 in the NFL.
Cheap ways to sample: $11 for one Tipsheet issue and $28 for a single Pregame play, and every write up is long by his own account (500 to 700 words a pick).
A clear niche: mostly totals, released the night before games so buyers can shop for a line.
concerns: The longer run is under 50%: 259-273-4 in NFL and college football on the Monitor from 2022 to now, with losing NFL seasons in 2022, 2024 and 2025.
Pregame shows hand picked slices of the record (all time NFL sides, this season's college totals) and a unit figure we could not reproduce.
The Tipsheet's "winning seasons in 15 of last 19 years" claim sits awkwardly with a forum tally of 45-45-1 for 2025, and the 2026 Team Total plays were 2-12 in that tally.
The Tipsheet's start year is given as 2005 in one Playbook paper and 2006 on the 2026 product page.
No guarantee or refund terms on the offers we read; Pregame's terms say its service is provided as is.
checklist: Look up the seller's full seasons on The Sports Monitor yourself before you buy. A hot month is not a record.
Ask Pregame or the seller which plays count toward the advertised units, and how many units each star rating means.
Count units, not wins. Star ratings change how much a 60% month is really worth.
Write down each pick the moment you receive it, with the total you can actually get. Totals move fast on game day.
Try one $11 Tipsheet issue or a single play before a $249 or $449 pass.
faq: Yes in the sense that it is a real, named seller: Victor King of King Creole Sports, a long time Playbook staff member, sells picks on Pregame and writes Playbook's NFL Totals Tipsheet. Whether the picks win is another matter. An outside tracker shows 259-273-4 in NFL and college football from 2022 to now, with a strong 2026 so far.
How much does King Creole cost?

On 19 Nov 2026 Pregame listed $119 for 7 days, $249 for 30 days, $449 for 90 days, $395 for the rest of the football season, $249 for the NFL only, $175 for college football only and $28 for a single NFL total. The Playbook NFL Totals Tipsheet was $59 for the 2026 season or $11 an issue.

The Sports Monitor of Oklahoma had him at 18-15 in the NFL and 23-8 in college football in 2026 through mid November. In 2025 it showed 33-44-1 in the NFL and 14-20-1 in college football. Pregame shows its own tables and +39.20 units for this football season.
What is the NFL Totals Tipsheet?

A weekly newsletter on NFL over/unders that Victor King writes for Marc Lawrence's Playbook. The 2026 product page says each issue has stats, trends and five best bets and goes out Tuesday afternoons. A TheRX member's tally at printed lines had it at 45-45-1 for 2025.
Does King Creole offer refunds or a guarantee?

We found none on the offers we read. Pregame's terms say its service is provided as is, and its FAQ mentions only an opposite side insurance program for buyers holding two handicappers on opposite sides of one game.

Not that we could find. On 19 Nov 2026 a WagerTalk profile address in his name sent us to the general experts page, and his name was not in WagerTalk's expert list. His picks were on sale on Pregame.com.
